briefTitle: Evaluation of Geriatric Assessment and Management for Older Adults With Non-small Cell Lung Cancer Receiving Chemotherapy Radiation Therapy

fuzzyCriteria.sourceText: Plan to start a new cancer treatment regimen within 4-6 weeks from time of baseline study visit. The treatment regimen is up to the discretion of the treating oncology physician.
fuzzyCriteria.reasonFuzzy: Treatment regimen is up to investigator discretion and involves complex scheduling and agent definitions.

fuzzyCriteria.sourceText: Presence of symptomatic brain metastases (if more than one) at time of study consent process. Patients with history of treated brain metastases or small indeterminate lesions (< 1cm) are eligible if they are not symptomatic at the time of study enrollment
fuzzyCriteria.reasonFuzzy: Brain metastases rules involve symptomatic status and multiple lesions rather than a simple clean allowedBrainMets category.

fuzzyCriteria.sourceText: More than one metastatic site: Examples: brain and adrenal, adrenal and liver
fuzzyCriteria.reasonFuzzy: Metastatic site counts and combinations require clinical judgment to assess.

fuzzyCriteria.sourceText: Stage III Lung Cancer AJCC v8

fuzzyCriteria.sourceText: Plan to start a new cancer treatment regimen within 4-6 weeks from time of baseline study visit. The treatment regimen is up to the discretion of the treating oncology physician.
fuzzyCriteria.reasonFuzzy: Treatment regimen is subject to investigator discretion and involves complex scheduling and agent definitions.

fuzzyCriteria.sourceText: Those patients with oligometastatic disease having only one site and one lesion outside of the radiation field will be eligible. Examples include a solitary brain metastasis (met), contralateral lung nodule or an adrenal metastatic site
fuzzyCriteria.reasonFuzzy: Oligometastatic disease criteria involve clinical judgment about lesion location, radiation fields, and specific sites.

fuzzyCriteria.sourceText: Able to provide informed consent, or if the oncology physician determines the patient to not have decision-making capacity, a patient-designated health care proxy (or authorized representative per institutional policies) must sign consent by the baseline visit
fuzzyCriteria.reasonFuzzy: Informed consent capacity assessment is subjective and depends on physician determination.

fuzzyCriteria.sourceText: Participant or healthcare proxy has adequate understanding of the English language (preferred) because not all GA measures have been validated in other languages.
fuzzyCriteria.reasonFuzzy: Language preference and translation availability are operational criteria rather than standardized clinical biomarker or stage filters.

fuzzyCriteria.sourceText: Have surgery planned within 3 months of approach date. Patients who have previously received surgery are eligible
fuzzyCriteria.reasonFuzzy: Planned future surgical procedures are subject to clinical scheduling and judgment.

fuzzyCriteria.sourceText: Presence of symptomatic brain metastases (if more than one) at time of study consent process. Patients with history of treated brain metastases or small indeterminate lesions (< 1cm) are eligible if they are not symptomatic at the time of study enrollment
fuzzyCriteria.reasonFuzzy: Symptomatic brain metastases wording involves clinical assessment of symptoms, lesion size, and treatment history.

fuzzyCriteria.sourceText: More than one metastatic site: Examples: brain and adrenal, adrenal and liver
fuzzyCriteria.reasonFuzzy: Evaluation of multiple metastatic sites requires clinical imaging interpretation.
